\section*{Frozen theorem contract}

Let $I$ be a directed set.  For $i\in I$, let $H_i\geq0$ be self-adjoint on
$\Hilb_i$, and let $H\geq0$ be self-adjoint on $\Hilb$ with
$\ker H=\mathbb C\vac$.  Let $\mathcal D\subset\vac^\perp$ be linear and
dense.  For every $x\in\mathcal D$, suppose that vectors $J_i x\in\Hilb_i$
are defined eventually and satisfy
\begin{align*}
 \langle J_i x,\e^{-tH_i}J_i x\rangle
   &\longrightarrow \langle x,\e^{-tH}x\rangle
   &&(t\geq0),\\
 \langle J_i x,\e^{-tH_i}J_i x\rangle
   &\leq M_x\e^{-mt}
   &&(t\geq0,\ i\succeq i_x),
\end{align*}
for one $m>0$ independent of $i$ and $x$, and some finite $M_x$.

\paragraph{Central conclusion.}
The target generator satisfies
\[
  \spec(H)\cap(0,m)=\varnothing.
\]
Thus a representation-specific Euclidean rigidity estimate becomes a target
spectral statement only through positivity, recovery of quadratic semigroup
forms, a centered dense core, and index-uniform decay.

\paragraph{Falsification conditions.}
The theorem is false as a mass-gap inference if the core is not dense, if the
target semigroup is not positive, if correlation recovery is absent, or if
the positive rates at finite index have zero infimum.  Exact countermodels
for density and uniformity accompany the proof.

\paragraph{Yang--Mills status.}
The theorem is an abstract transfer result.  Applying it to four-dimensional
Yang--Mills requires construction of continuum Schwinger functions, OS
positivity and reconstruction, a dense gauge-invariant centered core, and a
volume- and cutoff-uniform physical decay estimate.  Those inputs are not
proved in the manuscript.
